problems.title: The extra absolute-error loss is an empirical objective choice
problems.source_location: Proceedings Eqs.(7)–(13), PDF pp.5–6; Table 4, p.7; default loss weight, p.8
claim: The method adds an \(L^1\) term to squared RoI-velocity regression. The paper does not claim a formal exactness theorem for this augmented loss.
analysis: The distinction is real but does not refute a stated guarantee: with the paper’s \(\beta=2\) schedule, independent Gaussian initial RoI and target values \(1/4,3/4\) of probabilities \(3/4,1/4\), the conditional initial velocities are \(1/2-2r,3/2-2r\). Squared regression has mean minimizer \(3/4-2r\); adding scalar absolute-error weight \(1/5\) gives the unique minimizer \(7/10-2r\). This shows that the usual conditional-mean derivation does not automatically transfer to the modified objective. It does not establish an incorrect final distribution or degraded image quality. Table 4’s reported \(L^1\) ablation supports its empirical use.
result: No substantive error is established within this focused check. Retain the mean-versus-augmented-objective distinction as scope, without demanding removal of an empirically chosen loss.
problems.impact_rationale: The calculation contradicts an unstated exact-mean interpretation, not an actual theorem or measured image-generation result.
